products.title: Colombia Edinson Argote Lulo Kiwi Co-ferment
products.body_html:
Tastes like: Lulo, Kiwi, Mango

Light Roast | La Quebraditas Coffee Farm | Region: Huila, Colombia | Varietal: Castillo | Processing: Co-ferment with Lulo and Kiwi | Altitude: 1,800 MASL

Why This Coffee Stands Out

Edinson depulps the cherries dry, then submerges the beans in a mix of water, fermentation juice, and added yeast for a full 72-hour ferment — working in dried lulo and kiwi together, pairing two fruits rather than one to build a more layered co-ferment. He runs this at Quebraditas, his family's farm in Oporapa, Huila, where a naturally curious, experimental streak has shaped how he approaches processing. And the coffee comes from a producer who's still actively pushing the craft forward — Edinson runs Traditional, Experimental, and Fruit processing lines side by side at Quebraditas, so this Lulo Kiwi lot represents one live result of that ongoing R&D.

About Edinson Argote:

Edinson Argote is a passionate and resilient young coffee farmer from Huila, Colombia. Orphaned at just three and raised by his sister, he left home at 11 and later served in the army before discovering his true calling in specialty coffee while cupping beans at a local buying station. He subsequently worked on innovative farms in Cauca, rising to head of quality and processing control, before founding the family-run Quebraditas Coffee Farm with his partner, Luz Angela. There, at elevations between 1,600–1,850 m, he cultivates exotic varieties—including Ombligon—overseeing precision fermentation (thermal shock, yeast inoculation) alongside sustainable soil management practices.

products.body_html:
Award-winning Daye Bensa coffee in Sidama crafting high-altitude heirlooms with experimental processing, yielding vibrant berry jam, florals, and spice complexity

Tasting Notes: Grape, Blueberry, Jammy

Arbegona, Sidama, Ethiopia | Producer: Smallholder producers, WS - Daye Bensa

Varietal: Heirloom | Processing: Anaerobic Washed

Altitude: 1920–2330 MASL

About the Producers

Rumudamo is a renowned washing station in Arbegona, Sidama, operated by Daye Bensa Coffee and led by producer Asefa Dukamo. Set between 1,920–2,330 masl, the station works with over 600 smallholder farmers cultivating local heirloom varieties like 74112.

This region represents the forefront of Ethiopia’s quality movement — where meticulous cherry selection, high-elevation farming, and increasingly experimental processing techniques are redefining what Sidama coffees can express. Rumudamo, in particular, has built a reputation for consistency and innovation, regularly earning top placements in competitions and recognition for both washed and natural lots.

Why this coffee stands out

This Rumudamo lot captures the intersection of classic Sidama character and modern processing precision.

Expect a vivid, fruit-driven cup layered with blueberry and grape jam, supported by floral lift and a subtle spice complexity. The structure is juicy yet controlled, with a jammy sweetness balanced by bright, articulate acidity. Depending on the processing approach, there’s an added depth — a slightly fermented edge that enhances intensity without overwhelming clarity.

What makes this coffee compelling is its balance between power and refinement — a profile that delivers bold, expressive fruit while maintaining structure, elegance, and a clean, lingering finish.

products.title: India Ratnagiri Scoby Jasmine
products.body_html:
With vibrant notes of jasmine oil, coconut, and lavender, this coffee delivers remarkable aromatic complexity and structured acidity. It is processed using the same innovative fermentation approach as our beloved SCOBY coffee from Ratnagiri Estate, a coffee we’ve proudly carried for the past three years.

This new release introduces a new coffee called SCOBY Jasmine, developed by Mr. Ashok Patre and his team. Using a carefully selected yeast strain and lactic acid bacteria similar to a kombucha SCOBY, the fermentation enhances floral aromatics and layered sweetness while maintaining clarity in the cup.

The flavor profile evokes a familiar sensory tradition from South India—the pairing of jasmine flowers and coconut oil, long used in daily rituals and celebrations. In the cup, those aromas translate into an expressive and memorable coffee.

Expect an intense and complex aroma of jasmine and lavender, followed by bright acidity. As the coffee cools, the sweetness deepens with flavors of toffee, wildflower honey, and lingering florals.

A vibrant and complex blend featuring components from Ethiopia Layo Teraga, Edinson Argote’s Thermal Shock Sidra, and Diego Bermudez’s Cardamom Cloud. Created as Driftaway’s blend submission for the 2026 Roaster of the Year award, Peach Cobbler became the centerpiece of our winning box—scoring 90 and 91 points in evaluation. It may well be the greatest blend we’ve ever crafted.

Each component plays a vital role: the Layo Teraga brings a bright strong structure; Edinson's Sidra adds layered fruity complexity and sweetness; and Diego Bermudez’s Cardamom Cloud contributes spice depth and finish. Why This Coffee Stands Out

Sidra is a rare varietal grown at Quebraditas Coffee Farm in Huila, Colombia by Edinson Argote, a rising star in Colombia’s specialty coffee scene. After serving in the military, Edinson began working at his cousin’s washing station in Acevedo, where he discovered a passion for cupping and coffee quality. That early curiosity grew into a deep commitment, leading him to acquire Quebraditas with his partner Luz Angela.

Often compared to the celebrated Gesha varietal, Sidra is known for its floral, tea-like character and vibrant fruit notes—and has been featured in multiple World Barista Championship-winning routines. This lot underwent a Thermal Shock Washed process, a method that boosts clarity and complexity while unlocking an intensely fruit-forward profile.

Tastes like: Yellow fig, apricot, lemon

Region: Oromia, Guji Zone, Ethiopia | Varietal: 74110 | Processing: Washed | Altitude: 2,342 MASL

Nestled in Ethiopia’s highlands at 2,342 meters above sea level, the Layo Teraga Cooperative represents over 1,800 smallholder farmers in the Guji Zone. This meticulously crafted washed coffee captures Ethiopia’s signature clarity and vibrancy, with balanced sweetness and citrus brightness.

The cherries are hand-picked at peak ripeness, fermented for 12 days on raised beds, and washed clean to highlight the terroir’s natural elegance. The result is a cup that’s both lively and balanced, with lemony acidity and a silky mouthfeel.

Founded in 1976, the Layo Teraga Cooperative provides market access and training to smallholder members in Guji, helping them achieve higher quality and better income stability. Their focus on precision and care has made Layo Teraga one of Ethiopia’s most respected cooperatives.

products.body_html:
Tasting Notes: Milk Chocolate, Buttery, Malt

Country: Nicaragua | Region: Jinotega | Importer: Sucafina | Producer: 537 members of the SACACLÍ Cooperative | Processing: Washed | Altitude: 900–1,250 MASL | Varietal: Catimor, Catuai, Caturra, Maragogype, Marsellesa | Mill/Washing Station: On the farms


Our average cupping score: 85.5

About the Producers

The SACACLÍ Cooperative was founded in 1994 by 31 farmers, and since then its membership has grown to 537 members, 93 of which are women. They actually weren't growing coffee when they began, beginning operations in the coffee sector in 2008. By the 2017-2018 harvest, all member farms were certified Fairtrade and Regenerative Organic. SACACLÍ prioritizes environmental protection and community well-being. The group focuses on self-sustainable development, the continuous improvement of the quality of life for its members, and gender equity. Members have also implemented a range of practices on their farms including water conservation, soil management and agroforestry.

What makes this coffee stand out

SACACLÍ prioritizes environmental protection and community well-being. The group focuses on self-sustainable development, the continuous improvement of the quality of life for its members, and gender equity. In addition to coffee, the cooperative members also work with chili, tomato, and onion. Members have also implemented a range of practices on their farms including water conservation, soil management and agroforestry.

The cooperative grows their coffee using regenerative agriculture, which is the most effective tool that farmers have against deforestation, soil degradation, and varietal preservation. With a more stringent guidelines than Organic certification, Regenerative Organic aims to take the best parts of organic agriculture and build on it. Outlining the best practices for soil health, animal welfare, labor, and farmers, it combines all of these considerations into one standard.

About the Producers

The community of Patlanalan is one of the most remote communities in Puebla. Here, farmers grow coffee varieties like Mundo Novo and Yellow Caturra under native shade trees. Mundo Novo is a robust, high-yielding Brazilian hybrid of Bourbon and Typica, known for its strength and adaptability. Yellow Caturra is a natural mutation of the classic Bourbon-derived Caturra, celebrated for its excellent cup quality, manageable size, and the vibrant yellow cherries that give it both its name and visual distinction.


What makes this coffee stand out

Mundo Novo, Sarchimor, and Yellow Caturra represent distinct chapters in coffee cultivation. Mundo Novo is a robust, high-yielding Brazilian hybrid of Bourbon and Typica, known for its strength and adaptability. Sarchimor, a cross between Villa Sarchi and the rust-resistant Timor hybrid, is prized for its resilience against leaf rust and other diseases, making it a practical choice for challenging environments. In contrast, yellow Caturra is a natural mutation of the classic Bourbon-derived Caturra, celebrated for its excellent cup quality, manageable size, and the vibrant yellow cherries that give it both its name and visual distinction.

About the Producers

Ethiopia: The Gera Estate is located in the Dijmmah region of Ethiopia at high altitudes, encouraging slow cherry maturation that results in sweet, dense coffee seeds. The area also has nitrogen-rich plants and natural fertilizers (no chemical fertilizers or insecticides are used) that ensure delicious coffee production, focusing on sustainability and providing good working conditions for their employees. The Gera Estate provides childcare, education, housing, clean drinking water, electricity, healthcare, and recreational facilities for all of its employees free of charge.

Mexico: This lot is organized by former teacher Francisco Cortez, who has extensive knowledge in the local coffee-growing region. Perched in a canyon facing the Pacific, San Francisco Ozolotepec is a remote coffee-growing community in Oaxaca's Sierra Sur, located about eight hours by road from Oaxaca City. The name "Ozolotepec" comes from Aztec language and means "Hill of the Tiger." Humid climate and seasonal storms shape daily life and harvests. This lot unites five smallholders farming 1.5–2 hectares each, growing Typica, Caturra, and Oro Azteca. After harvest, cherries ferment 12–24 hours in tanks and bags, then dry on rooftop patios for about five days. 

What makes this coffee stand out

These two coffees come together to form a delicious and cohesive dark roasted coffee. Both coffees are naturally sweet, contributing to the vanilla notes in the final cup.

Why This Coffee Stands Out (our first competition lot!)

Ombligon is a rare Arabica varietal native to Huila, Colombia. Its name comes from the Spanish word “ombligo” (belly button), inspired by the bean’s distinctive shape. While its exact origins are unknown, it’s believed to be a natural mutation—possibly related to Ethiopian heirloom varieties.

What makes Ombligon truly special is its vibrant flavor profile: expect intense red fruit notes—like cherry cola, raspberry, and dark chocolate—balanced by a silky body and bright, juicy acidity. Its complexity and sweetness first gained attention at the 2023 World Barista Championship, where barista Jack Simpson used it across multiple beverage courses. More recently, this specific lot from producer Edinson Argote was featured by 2025 U.S. Barista Championship runner-up Isaiah Sheese and 2024 U.S. Brewers Cup 4th place finalist Josh Clements. 

Ombligon also offers practical advantages for producers: it’s naturally high-yielding, rust-resistant, and thrives at elevations of 1,600–1,800 m—making it increasingly sought-after in the specialty coffee world.

About Edinson Argote: 

Edinson Argote is a passionate and resilient young coffee farmer from Huila, Colombia. Orphaned at just three and raised by his sister, he left home at 11 and later served in the army before discovering his true calling in specialty coffee while cupping beans at a local buying station . He subsequently worked on innovative farms in Cauca, rising to head of quality and processing control, before founding the family-run Quebraditas Coffee Farm with his partner, Luz Angela. There, at elevations between 1,600–1,850 m, he cultivates exotic varieties—including Ombligon—overseeing precision fermentation (thermal shock, yeast inoculation) alongside sustainable soil management practices

  • Free shipping is via Amazon Shipping and takes 1–7 business days. For a more precise delivery date, we recommend upgrading to UPS.

    • Roast date listed: it’ll be intentionally rested for up to 14 days before shipping. These very light roasts benefit from extra rest.

Join a live tasting with James Hoffmann and other coffee enthusiasts

On October 3, James Hoffmann will host a live global tasting of the four coffees on YouTube. Brew along with him and coffee drinkers around the world as you taste the coffees side by side and explore how fermentation changes them. More info here.

About the Coffees

Same starting material, four different versions — built to show what fermentation actually does to a single lot. When people taste "fermented" coffees, they rarely get the un-fermented version alongside for comparison. This set gives you that control.

The four processing methods are:

1. Control — Mechanically Demucilaged (no fermentation) The baseline. Mucilage removed by machine, no microbes involved. This is the coffee's genetics and growing practices, unaltered.

2. Wild Fermentation A 48-hour submerged ferment with local, wild microbes — the traditional method most coffees go through, where whatever's already present breaks down the mucilage.

3. Lactobacillus (inoculated) A 48-hour submerged ferment with Lactobacillus. The bacteria enhance organic acid production, pushing brightness and complexity.

4. Saccharomyces Yeast (inoculated) A 48-hour submerged ferment with Saccharomyces yeast. The yeast enhances flavor precursors, shaping body and complexity.

This is an educational set — a conversation about the power and limits of controlled fermentation, not another extreme co-ferment.

About Lucia Solis & James Hoffmann:

Lucia Solis is a coffee fermentation consultant who came to coffee from wine — trained in viticulture and enology at UC Davis, with nine years in Napa winemaking before turning to coffee in 2014. She's since worked with producers in fifteen-plus countries, runs Luxia Coffee Solutions out of Guatemala, and hosts the Making Coffee podcast. This set was created with James Hoffmann — World Barista Champion and author — as part of The Fermentation Project: a single lot split into micro-lots using rigorous, tradition-rooted methods to reveal what fermentation genuinely changes.

products.title: Colombia Finca Milan Culturing Nitro Caturra
products.body_html:
Tastes like: Cantaloupe, Lemon zest, Raw Pineapple

Light Roast | Finca Milán | Region: Pereira, Risaralda, Colombia | Varietal: Caturra | Processing: Nitro Washed (nitrogen-purged bioreactor fermentation) | Altitude: 1,600 MASL

Why This Coffee Stands Out

This lot runs through Café Uba's signature "Nitro Washed" fermentation — one of the more controlled processes you'll find in Colombia. After pulping, the beans go into a sealed bioreactor with fruit must, starter cultures, and culturing lixiviates, and the whole atmosphere is purged of oxygen and flooded with nitrogen. That anaerobic environment lets Julio's team steer the microbes precisely, tracking temperature, pH, and Brix in real time to hold the ferment inside a narrow optimal window. The result is a clean, fruit-forward cup with a creamy body — cantaloupe and raw pineapple up front, bright lemon zest keeping it lifted. It's washed-coffee clarity with an added layer of engineered fruit, and it comes from a farm treating fermentation as active R&D rather than a fixed recipe.

About Finca Milán:

Finca Milán is a family-owned, 250-hectare estate in Pereira, Risaralda, led by third-generation producer Julio César Madrid Tisnés, whose family has farmed the land for over 40 years. Julio has turned Milán into one of Colombia's benchmark farms for experimental coffee, investing heavily in fermentation infrastructure and microbial research. He works closely with his daughter, a biologist, to study how specific microorganisms shape flavor — a collaboration that feeds directly into processes like this Nitro Washed lot. Alongside Caturra, the farm cultivates a deep bench of varieties including Castillo, Colombia, Bourbon Rosado, Bourbon Rojo, and Catiope. The work has earned recognition on the sport's biggest stage: coffees from this program have taken bronze and silver medals in back-to-back years at the World Barista Championship.

products.title: Colombia Franky Hoyos Tootsie Roll (Competition Series)
products.body_html:
A Collab release with Grind That Coffee!

Orange • Chocolate • Vanilla • Bubblegum

Finca El Encanto farm | Region: Pitalito, Huila | Varietal: Gesha | Processing: Yeast Inoculated | Altitude: 1550-1620 MASL

Tootsie Roll — Franky Hoyos Yeast-Inoculated Natural Gesha, Huila, Colombia

This coffee is a collab release with my competition coaches Hanna & Damian @grindthatcoffee — wonderful humans, exceptional coffee people.

Tootsie Roll is a yeast-inoculated natural Gesha from Franky Hoyos in Huila, Colombia — and the coffee our founder Suyog chose to represent Driftaway at the 2026 US Brewers Cup. Franky represents a new generation of producers: deeply rooted in tradition, and pushing the boundaries of what processing can do. Using thermal shock and precision yeast fermentation, he shapes flavor with an intention and clarity that's rare.

The result is a coffee that unfolds in distinct layers as it cools. When hot, expect chocolate-covered orange. As it warms, vanilla cream. When cool, it settles into bubblegum, with a long, coating finish. Sweetness is consistently high throughout — orange candy and cacao nib giving way to dark chocolate — and the mouthfeel moves from creamy to silky.

The name comes from the initial tasting notes — and a third flavor expression that only appears at a precise point of roast rest and extraction. This is one of the best coffees we've tasted in a long time, and we roasted this batch exactly the same way so you can experience what we served on the competition floor.

products.title: She Roars Espresso Blend
products.body_html:
Tasting Notes: Stone fruit, Toasted Almonds, Milk Chocolate

Turihamwe Turashobora & Ella Todos Santos Producer Groups | Region: Ngozi, Burundi & Huehuetenango, Guatemala | Varietal: Bourbon, Caturra, Catuaí, Pache, Yellow Pache | Processing: Washed | Altitude: 1,200–1,950 MASL

Why This Coffee Stands Out 

This is a classic, well-balanced espresso with plenty of depth. The chocolatey base gives it richness and structure, while subtle stone fruit brightness adds complexity without tipping into sourness. It’s smooth and forgiving — not too bitter, not too sharp — making it easy to dial in and consistently enjoyable.

She Roars holds up beautifully in milk, bringing out notes of milk chocolate and toasted almonds, but it’s just as satisfying on its own as a straight shot, where the balance and sweetness really shine.

About the Producers

She Roars is a 100% women-produced blend, sourced from women producers and producer groups across Guatemala and Burundi. Women play a critical role in coffee production worldwide, yet they are often underrepresented, underpaid, and overlooked in access to land ownership, financing, and direct market opportunities.

By intentionally sourcing this blend from women producers, we aim to help shift that imbalance and direct more value to the people whose labor and expertise shape the coffee. These coffees were selected not only for their quality, but for how beautifully they come together — creating a balanced, approachable espresso that reflects both craftsmanship and care at origin.

Recipe

• About 18 g of coffee with a 36 g yield (1:2 ratio)
• Target pull time of around 25–30 seconds for a well-balanced shot
• Make sure the coffee is rested for at least a week after roast — 10–14 days is even better

products.body_html:
An award-winning coffee — submitted as part of our 2026 Roaster of the Year win.

Tastes like:  Juicy Passionfruit, Candied Lychee, Jasmine petals

Light Roast | La Quebraditas Coffee Farm | Region: Huila, Colombia | Varietal: Sidra | Processing: Thermal Shock Washed | Altitude: 1,800 MASL

Why This Coffee Stands Out 

Sidra is a rare varietal grown at Quebraditas Coffee Farm in Huila, Colombia by Edinson Argote, a rising star in Colombia’s specialty coffee scene. After serving in the military, Edinson began working at his cousin’s washing station in Acevedo, where he discovered a passion for cupping and coffee quality. That early curiosity grew into a deep commitment, leading him to acquire Quebraditas with his partner Luz Angela.

Often compared to the celebrated Gesha varietal, Sidra is known for its floral, tea-like character and vibrant fruit notes—and has been featured in multiple World Barista Championship-winning routines. This lot underwent a Thermal Shock Washed process, a method that boosts clarity and complexity while unlocking an intensely fruit-forward profile.

About Edinson Argote: 

Edinson Argote is a passionate and resilient young coffee farmer from Huila, Colombia. Orphaned at just three and raised by his sister, he left home at 11 and later served in the army before discovering his true calling in specialty coffee while cupping beans at a local buying station . He subsequently worked on innovative farms in Cauca, rising to head of quality and processing control, before founding the family-run Quebraditas Coffee Farm with his partner, Luz Angela. There, at elevations between 1,600–1,850 m, he cultivates exotic varieties—including Ombligon—overseeing precision fermentation (thermal shock, yeast inoculation) alongside sustainable soil management practices

products.title: Colombia El Paraiso Cardamom Cloud
products.body_html:
Tasting notes: Cardamom, Pistachio, Butter

Both El Paraiso and this coffee need no introduction — this is likely Diego, Daniel and Alex Bermudez' finest work with Castillo, and the result is unlike anything we’ve ever tasted before. Balancing a cake-like sweetness with a cardamom-spice lift is nearly impossible in coffee, yet this lot does it effortlessly. We’re so happy and proud to serve it.

Grown at Finca El Paraíso in Piendamo at 1,960 meters, this Castillo lot showcases Diego’s signature precision in processing. After harvesting at peak ripeness, the cherries are ozone-washed and undergo a 72-hour double anaerobic fermentation, submerged in water with cultures in a milk medium. Once pulped, the coffee is combined with its own fermentation leachates to intensify aromatic precursors, followed by a thermal-shock wash that locks in complexity and sweetness.

The coffee is then dried in a dehumidifier to preserve its delicate aromatics and prevent over-oxidation. The result is a cup that’s floral, spiced, and radiant, with notes of cardamom and pistachio, wrapped in a soft, cake-like body — an exquisite example of the innovation and mastery coming out of Finca El Paraíso.

products.title: Mexico Paraiso
products.body_html:
Tasting Notes: Lemon, Red Apple, Molasses

Tenjolaya Ciwidey | Region: Chiapas, Mexico | Varietal: Caturra, Typica, Bourbon, Marsellesa | Producer: Several smallholder producers | Importer: Red Fox | Processing: Washed | Altitude: 1,350–1,800 MASL

Our average cupping score: 86.25

About the Producers

In the remote highlands of Nuevo Paraíso, Cafeco is more than a coffee project — it’s a movement. For the past four years, this dynamic team has worked alongside farmers to build infrastructure, resilience, and quality from the ground up. It began with a warehouse and a nursery, where Cafeco provides farmers with high-yield, rust-resistant coffee varieties to farmer partners free of charge. Now, they’re taking the next bold step: installing their own dry mill, funded by quality premiums, so farmers no longer face grueling journeys down rough mountain roads just to process their harvests.

What makes this coffee stand out

Chiapas is the heart of Mexico’s coffee industry, renowned for its exceptional coffee. Grown under the shade of lush canopy trees in rich volcanic soil, the beans develop a complex and nuanced flavor profile. What truly makes Chiapas coffee special, however, is the skill and dedication of its predominantly Indigenous farmers. Many of the indigenous communities who produce coffee today cultivate organically and through cooperatives, prioritizing sustainable practices that protect the region’s incredible biodiversity. This combination of ideal terroir and a commitment to environmental and social welfare results in a cup celebrated for its bright acidity and sweet notes.

products.title: India Chikmagalur Ratnagiri Washed
products.body_html:
A medium roasted coffee from smallholder farmers in India with tasting notes of praline, toast and brown sugar

TRACEABILITY

Country: India Region: Bababudangiri Chikmagalur Importer: Covoya Coffee Varietal: Catuai Caturra Producer: Ashok Patre Mill / Washing Station: Ratnagiri Estate Processing: Washed Altitude: 1200 - 1500 meters

PRODUCER'S STORY

Ratnagiri Estate is a 45 hectare (112 acres) farm established in 1920, and is currently owned and operated by Ashok Patre, having been passed down within his family for three generations.

Driftaway founders Anu and Suyog visited Mr. Patre in February of 2024, touring his farm and learning about the coffees and his process. Along with washed process coffees like this one, Mr. Patre produces natural and honey processed coffees. Drawing inspiration from other coffee origin countries, he steps beyond the boundaries of traditional Indian coffee cultivation and processing, conducting fermentation experiments, such as using anerobic methods he learned in Colombia.

Ratnagiri maintains Rainforest Alliance certification, and the estate itself is a lush and shaded environment with 3 stories of shade. Walking through the farm is like walking through a forest rather than over-cultivated fields. It is home to over 48 recorded bird populations, monkeys, leopards, wild boar, tigers, mongoose and - on occasion - elephants.

Mr. Patre uses organic fertilizer and compost to fertilize trees. The farm is fed by 2 freshwater streams, and he has implemented a strict protocol for processing wastewater before releasing it back into the environment. At intake, coffee fruit (cherry) is pulped on a mechanical Ecopulper that has reduced water use by 65%. The rich biodiversity demands that Mr. Patre and his family have an approach to farming which places ecology and harmony with the environment at the forefront.

products.title: Colombia Yoiner Mosquera Pink Bourbon
products.body_html:
Tasting Notes: Lemon, Strawberry, Dulce de Leche

On the Farm | Region: Huila, Colombia | Varietal: Pink Bourbon | Processing: Washed

Our average cupping score: 86.5

About the Producers

LaREB is a farmer-led collective of about 60 producers in Colombia, created to give smallholder growers direct access to international markets. By managing every step—from quality control and sales to financing, warehousing, and shipping—LaREB removes the need for intermediaries like exporters or importers. This structure means that most of the value of each coffee, around 80–90% of profits, stays in Colombia and goes directly to the producers who grew it.

One of those producers is Yoiner, a third-generation coffee grower who came to coffee after a career in banking and accounting. While working at Banco Agrario, he saw how difficult it was for small producers to succeed under the country’s financial system. Wanting to change that, he left the banking world to rebuild his family’s coffee farm, which he took over about six to eight years ago.

Yoiner’s early years were challenging—he experimented with buying cherries from nearby farms, a process that often lacked transparency and carried financial risk. After facing losses, he decided to focus instead on cultivating and processing coffee from his own land, where he could prioritize quality and traceability. His siblings remain active supporters, helping sustain the family’s long-standing coffee tradition as the farm continues to grow and evolve.

products.title: Bolivia Caranavi Rosita Geisha
products.body_html:
An elegant, high-elevation Geisha from Finca Rosita — refined, delicate, and quietly complex, showcasing the evolving identity of Bolivian coffee.

Tasting Notes: White Tea, Apricot, Sweet Cream

Caranavi, Bolivia | Producer: Valverde-Aramayo Family

Varietal: Geisha | Processing: Washed

Altitude: 1350–1740 MASL

About the Producers

Finca Rosita, located in the Illimani community in Caranavi, Bolivia, is part of the Valverde-Aramayo family’s legacy — named in honor of Rosa Angelica Aramayo, the family’s matriarch.

Set across 32 hectares dedicated entirely to coffee, the farm reflects both tradition and forward momentum. The region itself has undergone a remarkable transformation — from volume-focused production in the 1990s to a quality-driven movement supported by infrastructure, training, and generational change.

Today, Caranavi stands proudly as Bolivia’s “coffee capital,” with a new wave of younger producers pushing boundaries while staying rooted in strong agricultural traditions. Finca Rosita is a clear example of this shift — combining careful washed processing with high-elevation cultivation to produce coffees of clarity and distinction.

Why this coffee stands out

This Geisha leans into a more subtle and composed expression of the varietal — less about intensity, more about nuance.

Expect a soft, herbal-sweet profile with delicate florals and a tea-like structure. Notes of sweet grass and white tea lead, followed by gentle apricot and a light citrus lift. The texture is thin and buttery, with minimal acidity and a clean, sweet cream finish that lingers quietly.

What makes this coffee compelling is its restraint — a cup that rewards attention, revealing layers of sweetness and softness rather than overt brightness or intensity.

An expressive, high-elevation Typica Mejorado from Finca Hakuna Matata - showcasing the unmistakable character of this prized Ecuadorian varietal.

Tasting Notes: Berry, Lemon, Cane sugar

La Perla, Ecuador | Producer: Henry Gaibor and Verena Blasser.

About the Producers

Finca Hakuna Matata in Ecuador is owned and operated by Henry Gaibor and his wife, Verena Blasser. Located in La Perla, Nanegal, in the Pichincha region, they are a husband-and-wife team who moved from careers in medicine (surgeon and nurse) to cultivate high-quality coffee. They run the farm along with their nearby Finca Maputo, specialized in honey and washed, high-altitude coffee. 

Why this coffee stands out

Typica Mejorado is one of Ecuador’s most celebrated cultivars — a high-performing hybrid believed to be related to Ethiopian landrace material and improved Typica selections. It is prized for its pronounced florality, elevated sweetness, and layered fruit expression.

Of all the Typica Mejorados we’ve tasted over the years, this lot from Finca Hakuna Matata is among the best — complex, beautifully clear, and consistently high-scoring.

There are hints of mixed fruit, raspberry, and melon, with a texture that’s mouth-coating yet light, finishing with a touch of lemon that makes this lot unmissable.

Gloria Sepulveda | Region: Antioquia, Colombia | Varietal: Chiroso | Mill/Washing Station: Via Unblended | Importer: Unblended | Processing: Washed | Altitude: 1,700 MASL

About the Producers

Gloria Cecilia Sepulveda grows Chiroso on her one-hectare farm, El Porvenir, in Urrao, Antioquia — one of the regions putting Colombia's most exciting new varieties on the map. Gloria is a mentee of Carmen Montoya, the farmer who first put Chiroso on the global stage by winning the 2014 Cup of Excellence. Our sourcing partner, Unblended Coffee, works directly with Gloria to help her refine her processing and bring her coffee to roasters around the world. For Gloria, coffee is both a livelihood and a means to educate her children — that purpose shows up in every carefully processed lot.

What makes this coffee stand out

Gloria hand-picks only the ripest cherries and ferments them in open tanks for 36 hours before depulping and sun-drying on raised beds to 12% moisture. That careful, unhurried process is what gives this Chiroso its clean, distinctive character. Chiroso itself is a rare Ethiopian landrace variety that somehow found its way to the mountains of Antioquia, and at 2,000 meters it develops a complexity that punches well above its small farm size.

Hector Lopez | Region: Antioquia, Colombia | Varietal: Chiroso | Mill/Washing Station: Via Unblended | Importer: Unblended | Processing: Washed | Altitude: 2000 MASL

About the producer

Héctor López grows Chiroso on his five-hectare farm, El Susurro, in Pabón, a village in Urrao known for producing floral chirosos. After a 30-year career in textiles, Héctor retired and, inspired by two of his daughters who had already worked in coffee, moved to the countryside to start this new chapter with his family's support. He's since become a fixture in his community, offering neighbors internet access and support alongside his farming. This washed lot has notes of strawberry, plum and lime, with a creamy body. For Héctor, the farm is both a retirement project and a legacy — a way of putting down roots, literally and in his community.

What makes this coffee stand out

Héctor depulps each day's ripe cherries and layers them into the same open tanks all week, so Friday's batch ferments on top of Monday's, before the whole lot is washed together — a compounding process that builds unusual depth few producers attempt. El Susurro sits in Pabón, a village within Urrao specifically known for producing floral-leaning chirosos, giving this lot a distinct regional signature within the variety. And at five hectares with two employees, it's a notably larger operation than most Chiroso microlots, letting Héctor run this kind of multi-day, batch-building ferment at a scale few small producers can manage.

products.title: Colombia Jhon Didier Trujillo Chiroso Washed
products.body_html:
Tasting Notes: Wildflower Honey, Lemon Curd, Blackberry

Jhon Didier Trujillo | Region: Urrao, Antioquia, Colombia | Varietal: Chiroso | Mill/Washing Station: Villa Flor (on-farm) | Importer: Unblended | Processing: Washed | Altitude: 1950 MASL

Our average cupping score: 88

About the producer

Jhon Didier Trujillo grows Chiroso on Villa Flor, his 3.5-hectare farm near the Penderisco River in Urrao, the Antioquia municipality that has become synonymous with the variety. For Jhon Didier, farming has always been about more than coffee — it's how he provides for his family and builds something that will outlast him. Alongside coffee he grows lulo, avocado and plantains and keeps dairy cattle, a diversified farm that gives the family stability through the swings of the coffee market. His son Juan Camilo has now joined him, and together they share a vision of Villa Flor as a sustainable, profitable business for generations to come. This washed lot is layered and honey-sweet, with bright lemon acidity, a run of blackberry and raspberry, and a buttery, custard-like finish.

What makes this coffee stand out

Chiroso is prized for its floral, tea-like delicacy, but this lot brings unusual weight to the cup — a buttery body and lingering dulce de leche sweetness that sit underneath the classic citrus and berry brightness, so it drinks like a Chiroso with the volume turned up. Villa Flor sits at 1,950 metres beside the Penderisco River, whose steady water supply and cool, humid microclimate slow cherry maturation and give Jhon Didier consistent fermentation conditions season after season. For us, this tastes like a Kenyan coffee but from Colombia!

products.title: Rwanda Kilimbi Anaerobic Natural
products.body_html:
Tasting Notes: Red Wine, Strawberry Jam, Dark Chocolate

Kilimbi Washing Station (750 smallholder farmers) | Region: Nyamasheke, Western Province, Rwanda | Varietal: Red Bourbon | Mill/Washing Station: Kilimbi CWS | Exporter: Muraho Trading Company | Importer: [Importer] | Processing: Anaerobic Natural | Altitude: 1650–1850 MASL

Our average cupping score: 87.50

About the producer

Kilimbi sits on the shores of Lake Kivu in Nyamasheke District, in Rwanda's Western Province, and was the first washing station Muraho Trading Company built when the company launched in March 2016. Under station manager Radjab Mvuyekure and a core team of four full-time staff, Kilimbi receives cherry from around 750 smallholder farmers in the surrounding hills, processing 300 to 350 tonnes a year across washed, natural and honey lots. Some farmers deliver their cherry by boat across the lake — a daily reminder of how closely the station's life is tied to Kivu. This anaerobic natural lot is dense and winey, with a deep strawberry-jam sweetness, and a dark-chocolate, mouth-coating finish.

What makes this coffee stand out

For decades Rwandan law required all export coffee to be fully washed, and Kilimbi, together with its sister station Rugali, was the first station in the country's history to legally produce and export natural and honey processed coffee. It went on to become the first Rwandan station to successfully produce black and red honey lots, so the experimental processing behind this coffee is not a trend Kilimbi adopted — it's a tradition the station created. In an anaerobic natural, whole ripe cherries ferment in sealed, oxygen-deprived tanks before being dried slowly on raised beds, which pushes the fruit toward the wine-like, jammy intensity you taste here while keeping the cup clean and structured. Kilimbi's mid-altitude lakeside setting, with the moderating influence of Lake Kivu on temperature and humidity, gives the station unusually steady drying conditions for this kind of high-risk process, and its lots have gone on to feature in multiple barista competitions.

products.body_html:
Black Honey Mossto Lactic Sudan Rume, Enigma Hops Co-ferment

Edwin Enrique Noreña — Finca Campo Hermoso

Competition Series

Tasting Notes: Piña colada, Key lime pie, Kiwi, Peach candy, Clove

Varietal: Sudan Rume | Processing: Black Honey (carbonic maceration lactic fermentation, co-fermented with Enigma Hops)

Altitude: 1,600 MASL | Farm: Finca Campo Hermoso | Region: Armenia, Quindío

About the Producer

Edwin Noreña is a 3rd-generation coffee producer at Finca Campo Hermoso, a trained agronomist, certified Q-grader, and sought-after Cup of Excellence judge — a rare combination of inherited craft and formal expertise.

Quality and repeatability are his hallmarks. Edwin has developed an extraordinary following for his mastery in fermentation and co-fermentation, borrowing techniques from the wine and beer industries to build recipes with an everlasting sweetness. His ultimate goal: to make coffee approachable enough that you don't need a professionally trained palate to find what's in the cup.

Why this coffee stands out

This Campo Hermoso lot captures Edwin's signature precision at its most expressive. The Sudan Rume variety brings inherent brightness and a delicate floral structure, while the black honey process and Enigma Hops co-fermentation layer in tropical fruit complexity and a creamy, lingering sweetness.

Expect creamy aromatics on the nose, piña colada and key lime in the body, and peach candy on a clean, extended finish. The cup keeps unfolding as it cools — every sip reveals something new. Bold and expressive, yet structured and refined.

First cupped in August 2024 and brought to the 2025 competition menu, this is a coffee that raises expectations.
